newsitem.title: HONG KONG: GITIC Enterprises to offer 100 mln new shrs in IPO.
newsitem.headline: GITIC Enterprises to offer 100 mln new shrs in IPO.

text.p: China-backed GITIC Enterprises Ltd is seen issuing 100 million new shares at HK$1.05 each in an initial public offering (IPO) of shares in Hong Kong, market sources said on Tuesday.
The issue price will represent a prospective price to earnings multiple of 9.2 times on a fully-diluted basis and 7.7 times on a weighted average basis, they said.
"The shares are expected to be offered solely to Hong Kong investors and there is no international placement," an analyst said after attending a company presentation on Tuesday.
The IPO is expected to run from March 17-20, with dealing in the shares expected to begin on March 26, sources said.
Goldwyn Capital Ltd is expected to be the sponsor of the issue, they said.

GITIC Enterprises, a Hong Kong-based construction materials distributor, is indirectly controlled by Guangdong International Trust and Investment Corp (GITIC), the investment arm of the government of the southern Chinese province of Guangdong, they said.

Of the HK$95 million in net proceeds from the issue, about HK$54 million would be used to buy machinery for the second phase of development of a construction material plant at Huado in Guangdong province and HK$7 million for its construction, sources said.

About HK$18 million would be used to expand the company's construction materials' distribution network in Hong Kong and Guangdong, with the remaining HK$16 million used for repayment of short-term bank borrowings and for working capital, they said.
"The company forecasts its profit to rise to HK$42.7 million for the year ended in December 1996 on an estimated turnover of HK$332.3 million," another analyst said.

The company posted a profit of HK$35.8 million in 1995, HK$35.7 million in 1994 and HK$24.8 million in 1993. Turnover was HK$275.4 million in 1995, HK$240.6 million in 1994 and HK$173.3 million in 1993, they said.
The marble and granite products trader reported a profit of HK$33.9 million for the first 10 months of 1996 on turnover of HK$257 million, sources said.
"Construction materials business accounted for about 71 percent of the company's turnover, and the remaining 29 percent was from its rental property portfolio," one source said.
Sources said the company owned a 12,000-square-foot warehouse in Yuen Long in Hong Kong's New Territories and a 264,000-square-foot warehouse in Guangdong.
The company also holds 8,976 square metres of floor space in a shopping arcade in GITIC Plaza, a commercial complex in Guangzhou owned by its parent, sources said.
